glosses: To make clear or effective.
To speak clearly; to enunciate.

examples.text: I wish he’d articulate his words more clearly.

glosses: To explain; to put into words; to make something specific.

examples.text: I like this painting, but I can’t articulate why.

glosses: To bend or hinge something at intervals, or to allow or build something so that it can bend.

examples.text: an articulated bus

glosses: To attack a note, as by tonguing, slurring, bowing, etc.

examples.text: Articulate that passage heavily.

glosses: To form a joint or connect by joints.

examples.text: The lower jaw articulates with the skull at the temporomandibular joint.

glosses: To treat or make terms.

examples.text: Send us to Rome / The best, with whom we may articulate / For their own good and ours.

glosses: Clear; effective.
Speaking in a clear and effective manner; having both good articulation and good elocution.

examples.text: She’s a bright, articulate young woman.

glosses: Consisting of segments united by joints.

examples.text: jointed articulate animals
The robot arm was articulate in two directions.

glosses: Distinctly marked off.

examples.text: an articulate period in history

glosses: Expressed in articles or in separate items or particulars.

examples.text: articulate sounds

glosses: Related to human speech, as distinct from the vocalisation of animals.

examples.text: Brutes cannot form articulate Sounds, cannot articulate the Sounds of the Voice, excepting some few Birds, as the Parrot, Pye, &c.

examples.text: Plusieurs fois, des écrivains éloquents crurent qu'ils pourraient déterminer un courant de réaction contre ces doctrines, […].
